_note: Quests (docs/design/quests_levels_story.md section 5). Every number is a [PLACEHOLDER]. Read by scripts/quests/quest_engine.gd, which only watches what GameState already keeps. A quest: kind (story, lab, personal, daily), giver (a cast id), title, scope (farm, or player: each player's own, kept on the farm and in a guest's own file), gates (lab_level, band, skill {id, level}, total_level, quest_points, quest_done: all must hold), offer (when: always, day_at_least with day, or any step check with its fields), offer_line (what the giver says with the offer: a path in dialogue_dispatches.json or the line itself), steps (in order unless any_order is true) and rewards (credits, lab_xp, xp_<skill id>, quest_points, xp_certificate, phone: a path in dialogue_dispatches.json or the line itself). xp_certificate is the XP one certificate is worth: each player who took part is given one and spends it on one skill of their own (SKILLS, K). It is sized to the quest, not the player, so the 10 % curve makes it lift a low level a lot and a high level a little. A step: id, text, check and its fields, at_least (1 if left out). The count and counter checks count from the day the quest was accepted unless ever is true. In a quest done in order, a later count or counter step counts from when the step before it was done (unless ever is true), so what is done early is not counted for a later step. Checks: stat_at_least (stat), flag (flag), band_at_least (band), owns_standard (standard_id), lab_size, count (log, where), state_is (state, is: one value or a list), level (skill: a skill id, lab or total), counter (counter: a source id of data/skills.json, or crops_sold_in_spec with where { crop_id }: what Lin has bought in spec). A step may carry minigame (a mini-game's id; set_the_zero is the one there is): it must be a count of cal_log rows whose where names one instrument_id, and while it is the quest's open step the bench opens that game for that instrument, on a farm that has calibrated its kind before too. The step is done by its check alone, so a skip or a poor try does it as a plain calibration does. A score of 60 or more is kept with the step; when the quest is paid, Fine (80) adds 10 % of the quest's credits and Reference (95) adds 20 % [ASSUMPTION], and at Reference the giver also says the step's minigame_line (a path in dialogue_dispatches.json or the line itself). Lab and daily quests pay no quest points. closed_when (when: a step check with its fields): a quest that was never offered is marked done with nothing paid once this holds, for an offer that can no longer come. A quest id and a step id are kept in saves and must never be renamed; a quest must have steps, each a dictionary with its own id. A quest may have endings (a list of { id, when and that check's fields, phone }): when it is paid, the giver says the phone line of the first ending whose check holds, in place of the reward's phone; an ending's when is always, day_at_least or a step check, and is looked at before the quest is paid; every ending pays the same, and which one it was is not kept. The count logs are cal_log, job_log, audit_log, certificates and oirm_trips. Quests are offered each morning and when a farm is opened, not after a command. The lab-level gates of the design's unlock table are not here: they wait for build step 9. any_gate (a list of gates dictionaries): at least one of them must hold, beside gates, which must all hold; this is how a quest says 'credibility 20, or lab level 6'. The gate credibility is the farm's credibility points. A farm's quest may have a job: a job as data/economy.json's templates are (id, customer, item, discipline, min_tier, pay, due_in_days, bench_minutes; no min_band and no area), handed out by the quest into active_jobs and never on the board, with the quest's id on it and on its job_log row (quest). It is handed out when the quest is offered, whatever the lab can do yet, and again on any morning or farm opening that finds the quest open with no such job accepted and no such row in job_log, so a job that ran out or was dropped comes back as often as it takes (the giver then says job_again_line); a quest's job that runs out costs no credibility. A job with flat_cut_pct is cut once by that much when it is late, untraceable or both, in place of the board's two cuts; the credibility points and the job XP are a board job's. The check quest_job (quest: the quest's id) is 1 once that job is accepted or done. S3's envelope, its 200 CR, its half, the three days and the pressure gauge are [PLACEHOLDER]. A quest of kind daily is a daily ask (section 6, D2): scope player, no quest points, and one a day for each player. Each morning (and when a farm is opened, or a guest comes in) a player who holds none of today's is given one of the asks whose gates and offer hold for them, picked by the farm's seed, the day and the player, so host, guest and reload agree. Its entry sits with the player's own quests and `accepted` is its day; an ask of another day is taken out on the next look, done or not, with nothing paid and nothing lost, and can be asked again. The offer is posted as the giver's line and 'Today's ask:' with the step. Counting starts when the ask is given. A counter step with whose: farm counts every player's doing, in a player's own quest too: the asks about what the farm shares (Orin's row on the plot, Bram's ore from the fissures) use it, with an offer that needs enough left (plot_untilled, fissures_open), so another player using the plot or the fissures moves the ask on and never puts it out of reach. A daily ask does not travel in a guest's file, and its XP certificate is given every time it is done and stays on the farm that gave it. Two checks for offers: found_blocks (how many reference blocks the farm has dug up) and plot_untilled (how many plot cells are still to till), so an ask that could not be done is not picked. The counter check_with_block:<instrument id> is a player's checks of that instrument against a block (GameState.check_with_block; it gives no XP). daily_lin_reeds counts what Lin bought from the whole farm, as crops_sold_in_spec always does. The asks' sizes, the 30 to 60 CR and the 25 XP certificate are [PLACEHOLDER].

steps.text: Pass an audit with no findings.
Finish the OIRM contract's run of on-time calibrations.
Calibrate the soil probe against the gravimetric kit.
Sell Lin a crate of in-spec dust turnip.
Have your first audit on file.

job.item: a pressure gauge that will not read right

steps.text: Take the envelope job from under the airlock.
Calibrate the gauge at the bench and hand it back.
Sell Lin three in-spec Biscuit Reeds.
Mine two fissures for crystal ore.
Check the rover's steering encoder against a reference block.
Till six cells of the plot.
